title: Synchronous FIFO
constraints: Writes when full and reads when empty are ignored. `full` and `empty` are evaluated before the clock edge.
`dout` is registered: it changes only on a clock edge with a successful read (or on reset, to 0).
hints: Use an 8-entry memory as a circular buffer with a write pointer and a read pointer.
3-bit pointers wrap on their own. To tell full from empty, keep a separate count or give the pointers a 4th bit.
Compute `do_wr = wr_en && !full` and `do_rd = rd_en && !empty` first, then update the pointers, the count and `dout` from those.

examples.title: fill
examples.expected: count = 1 … 8, empty drops after the first write, full = 1 after the 8th

examples.title: drain
examples.expected: dout = 0xA0, 0xA1, … 0xA7, count = 7 … 0, empty = 1 at the end

examples.title: read + write together
examples.input: write 0x11 / 0x22 / 0x33 with rd_en = 1 on an empty FIFO, then one more read
examples.expected: dout = 0x11, 0x22, 0x33 (each read returns the value written just before)
